chart_review.key_findings: Dolores Ramirez is a 54-year-old Hispanic woman with early-onset Alzheimer's disease (G30.0 / F02.80) on combined donepezil 10 mg HS + memantine 10 mg BID. Her MoCA trajectory in the chart is 22 (2024-07-15) -> 20 (2025-01-08) -> 18 (2025-07-21) -> 16 (2025-11-15) -> 14 (2026-02-20). She is on 19 active medications including 2 high-risk agents (lorazepam 0.5 mg PRN added 2025-12-08 in the ED, quetiapine 12.5-25 mg HS PRN added 2026-01-15). She has 2 ED visits in the past 12 months (5/12/2025 unwitnessed bathroom fall; 12/8/2025 sundowning agitation), Morse Fall Scale 55 (2026-02-20), Z63.6 caregiver-burden problem-list entry added 2025-09-10, Zarit-12=22 documented in the social work assessment, hemoglobin 12.4 -> 11.8 trend, and PHQ-9 13 / GAD-7 11 on most recent screening.
chart_review.clinical_interpretation: Early-onset Alzheimer G30.0/F02.80 is uncontrolled (§2.2): MoCA 14 (<18), Morse 55, fall/unsafe-alone concerns. Authored pan-left-on and navigation difficulties ground home-safety planning.
chart_review.risk_rationale: Retain the task-authored risk designation under risk-stratification §3.1–§3.3, supported by the numeric referral/utilization/clinical anchors in key_findings; medication class or a single disease-control band does not replace the combined risk framework.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Hello, I am Alex, a care manager with The Healthcare Company. Is this a private and suitable time for a brief explanation?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Please ask me, and slow down. Carlos does not answer for me.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: I will speak to you directly, slow down, and check whether my explanation was clear without quizzing your memory. Carlos is optional support only if you ask for him; your own choice controls enrollment. Would a brief explanation in that scope be okay?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: A brief explanation is okay. Please let me choose what I answer.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Care management helps coordinate support with your care team. It is voluntary, has no separate program fee, and you can stop at any time. Joining does not change your benefits or give someone else your decisions.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: What would you actually help with?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: We could organize medication and home-safety supports and coordinate one low-burden follow-up while you remain in charge. I can check options and coordinate, but cannot guarantee access, approval, cost reductions, or a clinical outcome. Would that kind of process help be useful?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: That sounds more useful. I still want to understand who sees what I say.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: I can use chart and call information to organize care-management support. Relevant information is documented for the care team; I will explain any proposed wider sharing. Privacy has safety and legal limits, including urgent danger; I cannot promise absolute secrecy. May we start only with what would make this call respectful?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes, that topic is okay. Please go slowly.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: What feels hardest about that, in your own words? You can leave details private.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I sometimes mix up pills, and it is embarrassing when Carlos notices.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Memory changes can make a rushed call feel like losing your voice. I will ask you directly, leave time, and include Carlos only if you invite him.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you for hearing that. I do not want this to turn into a checklist.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: We can work on one concern at a time and stop whenever you choose. Enrollment does not require all your personal details today. Is there something you want this support to help you do?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I want Carlos supported without people treating him as the boss of my care.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: We can make that your priority. A first step would be to organize medication and home-safety supports and coordinate one low-burden follow-up while you remain in charge. These are coordination steps, not a promise that the problem will be solved on this call.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Can I decide later about a referral or family involvement?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes. Each referral, family contact, and new sensitive topic needs its own discussion. You can skip a question or stop the program. A request for information alone is not enrollment consent.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I understand. I would like a manageable follow-up call.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Would telephone follow-up be acceptable? We can agree a convenient time at each contact; please tell me before any other person is included.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Telephone is okay. Please arrange the next time with me and ask before involving anyone else.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Before you decide: this is voluntary care-team coordination, with no separate program fee, the information-use and safety limits we discussed, your chosen contact arrangements, and the right to stop. What would you like clarified?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: That answers my questions. I understand that you can check options but cannot promise the result.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: With those boundaries and the first step we discussed, do you clearly agree to enroll in care management today?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes, I agree to enroll today on those terms.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Enrollment is your choice. Would you like to continue with one practical topic now, with a pause after each, or stop for today?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I choose to continue one topic at a time. I may still skip optional details.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: I will start with the charted treatment routine and follow-up, then ask your permission before each personal question. The chart is a starting point; it does not tell me how things are going for you now.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: That is okay. Please ask one specific question and give me time.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: May I ask about one recent home-safety difficulty? I will leave time and will not quiz you. This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I left a pan on once and got turned around near the store. Please slow down instead of quizzing me.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: May we talk about keeping morning and evening pills straight? This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have mixed up morning and evening pills. I feel embarrassed when Carlos notices.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Would you like Carlos involved as support, while I continue asking you first? This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Carlos may listen if I say yes, but ask me first. I do not want him treated as the boss of the call.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Safety concerns may require care-team help. May I ask how the memory slips affect mood and whether you are trying to hurt yourself? This helps tailor support. You may skip or stop.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I get anxious and ashamed when my memory slips. I am not trying to hurt myself.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: Thank you. I will keep that specific to what you chose to share. Would you like a pause before another topic?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: I have enough energy to continue with the next separate topic.

ideal_dialogue.speaker: care_manager
ideal_dialogue.message: You do not need to give optional stories, exact finances, locations, or family details. Shall we leave those private and review the support you selected?

ideal_dialogue.speaker: patient
ideal_dialogue.message: Yes. Leave those optional details private for now.
